rationale.conceptual: The agent only needs to translate given closed-form expressions for |T|², wavefunction, and dipole moment into code, then compute an FFT. This is a standard numerical task (numpy, scipy) with minor physical interpretation, not the deep non-perturbative derivations of the paper.
rationale.execution: The workflow has two logical stages (transmission probability → harmonic spectrum) but they are trivially combined; the reference solve.sh uses a single script, and the scoring step is essentially one computation with a helper. No complex tooling or fragile orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task asks to compute a harmonic emission spectrum using explicitly provided analytic formulas for transmission amplitudes and a given wave packet. The method is a straightforward numerical Fourier transform; the intellectual challenge of the underlying theory (integrability, form factors) is abstracted away, leaving only plug-in arithmetic. The pipeline is short (transmission probability helper plus spectrum computation). Resource needs are minimal CPU and memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: CPU-only: time–space grids are small (~6000 time points, ~300 spatial points), only numerical integration and FFT, no large external data.
